transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Nice to meet you. Um, well, I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble at work lately. I'm a construction manager, and... well, it's probably not a huge deal, but I wanted to get it checked out just to be safe. Is that okay? 

Basically, I'll be starting a safety briefing with the guys, or going over a plan review, and I really try my best to pay attention. But then, almost right away, my mind just sort of wanders off to, you know, three other problems on the job site. And then I end up missing things that I know I should have caught. It's just a little distracting, I guess. Am I explaining that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed this kind of difficulty focusing your whole life, even back in school, or is this something that's started more recently?

Well, I guess... yeah, it's kind of been my whole life, really. I hope it's okay to go way back, but, um, even in elementary school, my teachers were already telling my parents about it. 

I wasn't trying to be a bad kid or disrespectful or anything, I promise. But they'd say I had a hard time staying in my seat, and that I talked out of turn a bit. Just getting a little too eager, I suppose? And they mentioned I'd lose my homework, or I'd sort of rush through the directions on assignments before I really understood what they wanted me to do. It wasn't that I didn't care, I just... always kind of jumped the gun, I guess. 

Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of background.
When your mind wanders during those briefings, is it because you're preoccupied with worrying about things going wrong, or does it just drift to unrelated thoughts without a sense of worry?

Um, well, it's not really worrying, I don't think. I mean, I care about the job, obviously, and I want things to go right. But it's not like I'm sitting there panicked or anything. 

It's more just... my brain sort of hops around. Like, I'll be looking at the safety sheet, and then I'll remember the concrete truck is coming at noon, and then I'll wonder if we ordered enough rebar, and then I'm thinking about if I need to pick up dog food on the way home. It's just kind of... busy up there. Not anxious, just... bouncing around. Is that normal? I hope that makes sense. I just want to make sure I'm explaining the difference right.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong pattern (since elementary school) of inattention (mind wandering during tasks, missing important details, losing homework, difficulty sustaining attention) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (difficulty staying seated, talking out of turn, rushing through directions), consistent with combined presentation ADHD. Symptoms are not better explained by anxiety, as the patient explicitly denies worry-based distraction and describes non-anxious, rapid thought-shifting. Current occupational impairment (missing safety details at work) confirms functional impact, and childhood onset with cross-situational persistence (school and now work) supports the diagnosis of ADHD combined type rather than a primarily inattentive or hyperactive-impulsive subtype, or an anxiety disorder.
